Auto-summary (auto-generated):

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick rollcall — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and we have Ethan from SE on to cover the technical stuff.
[00:12] Alex: Hi, Alex here. Priya, Jordan as well — thanks for doing this, we want to validate your posture before we move to pilot.
[00:20] Maya: Great. The goal today is to show you where our SOC 2 and ISO artifacts live, how to get read-only access to the Trust Center, and talk through controls mapping and a short walkthrough of audit logs and KMS options.
[00:31] Priya: Awesome. High level questions up front: do you provide a consolidated control mapping for SOC2/ISO so we don't have to do the heavy lift? And second, how do you handle audit logs for EU-hosted tenants?
[00:43] Ethan: Yep, good questions. We have an internal controls matrix that maps our SOC 2 Type II controls to the ISO 27001 clauses — we can share a redacted version. For EU tenants, logs are retained in EU regions by default when the tenant is provisioned in an EU zone; export and S3-style archival is supported.
[00:58] Jordan: When you say exported — is it on-demand or behind a support ticket? What format?
[01:04] Ethan: You can do on-demand exports through the Console for audit logs (JSON/ndjson) and also via the audit-logs API for automated pulls. For some archive workflows we recommend configuring a dedicated S3 bucket and a lifecycle policy.
[01:18] Priya: And who can access those exports? Our auditor will want a read-only bucket access pattern.
[01:24] Maya: RBAC covers that. In the Trust Center and Console we have roles that map to read-only auditor roles. We'll share the Trust Center permissions guide with exact role names.
[01:34] Alex: Can you show the Trust Center quickly? We only need view access to artifacts, not admin.
[01:40] Maya: Sure — Ethan, do you want to share the Trust Center screenshot and link?
[01:44] Ethan: I'll paste the link in chat: https://trust.redwood.ai/trust-center/ql-demo (note: demo link). Ok, first panel shows SOC 2 Type II report summary — it includes scope, period, and auditor statement.
[01:58] Priya: Are those full reports downloadable or just summaries? Auditors ask for the control narratives sometimes.
[02:04] Ethan: For customers under NDA we can provide the full SOC 2 Type II report PDF and ISO 27001 certificate; the Trust Center will surface summaries and a request flow to obtain the full artifact.
[02:14] Alex: What's the turnaround on a full report request?
[02:17] Maya: Typically 1–3 business days after the access request and NDA confirmation; for enterprise contracts it's often pre-provided as part of onboarding.
[02:26] Jordan: KMS — how does key management work if we want to use our own key in EU?
[02:31] Ethan: We support customer-managed keys via major cloud KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault). For private deployments we can support HSM or on-prem KMS integrations as part of the Private package. The managed-hosted flow uses envelope encryption where your CMK is used to wrap the data keys.
[02:48] Priya: Is there a BYOK flow in the Hosted product or only in Dedicated/Private?
[02:52] Ethan: Hosted supports CMK for data at rest in the provider regions; the Dedicated/Private options offer stronger isolation and dedicated networking if you need the KMS entirely under your control.
[03:05] Alex: On controls mapping — do you have the mapping template in Excel or a machine-readable format?
[03:10] Maya: We normally provide a spreadsheet (XLSX) with columns for control ID, our internal control description, evidence artifacts, and where to find them in the Trust Center. We can export CSV on request.
[03:22] Priya: Can you pre-fill the ones that are in-scope for our use case? That would save weeks.
[03:27] Maya: Yes, if you provide your control list we'll pre-map the overlapping controls and mark where evidence is available. We won't do customer-specific evidence collection, but we will indicate what artifacts can be exported or shared.
[03:40] Alex: We need mapping to ISO 27001 Annex A controls plus SOC control IDs — our audit team wants a side-by-side.
[03:47] Ethan: That's standard; we'll attach the mapping and highlight controls that require configuration on your side (SSO, RBAC, data retention).
[03:54] Jordan: A note on SSO — we run Azure AD, and need IdP-initiated SAML with SCIM for group sync. Any blockers?
[04:02] Ethan: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning for groups and user sync. There's a small config in the Console to enable SCIM and map groups to RBAC roles.
[04:11] Priya: What's the granularity of RBAC? Can we create an auditor role that can only view logs and export, but not see customer data or prompt history?
[04:20] Maya: Yes, the RBAC model separates admin, developer, billing and auditor scopes. Prompt history and full content access can be toggled; we can demonstrate the exact role permissions in the demo.
[04:31] Alex: Logging retention — our policy is 3 years for certain controls. You mentioned lifecycle to S3, but can you guarantee immutability / WORM for auditors?
[04:41] Ethan: Immutability is supported via S3 object lock if you use your own archival bucket and enable object lock there. For hosted-managed buckets we can provide time-limited retention guarantees and write-once workflows upon request, but for full legal hold we advise export to your own bucket with object lock enabled.
[05:00] Priya: Any PII redaction or masking in logs by default?
[05:04] Ethan: We do not automatically redact content in request logs because customers' need varies. However, we have configurable redaction pipelines (token-level masking) you can enable, or we can help set up a pre-export filter.
[05:15] Alex: For EU data residency — if we provision a tenant in eu-west-1, will any metadata ever cross to US for control plane reasons?
[05:23] Maya: The control plane handles global account management but we can restrict artifact storage and logs to EU regions. We have contractual terms for data residency in enterprise contracts. The control plane may hold minimal telemetry for billing; we can scope that in the contract.
[05:38] Jordan: How are audit logs indexed? Searchable via Console or only raw export?
[05:43] Ethan: Searchable via Console with timeframe filters; for large-scale forensic work we recommend raw exports and Elastic-compatible ingestion.
[05:50] Priya: Any specifics about ISO scope — do you cover model inference infrastructure in your ISO certificate?
[05:56] Ethan: Yes, our ISO 27001 scope includes the inference runtime and hosting services used for the hosted offering; we will share the scope statement.
[06:05] Alex: Okay, helpful. Can we talk about evidence collection during a SOC 2 audit — what artifacts are typical?
[06:11] Ethan: Typical artifacts: configuration screenshots, access logs, change management records, incident response runbooks, evidence of backups, KMS usage logs, and contractual agreements for subservice organizations. We can diagram where each artifact lives in the Trust Center and what we can supply.
[06:26] Priya: Any known gaps we should watch for?
[06:29] Maya: The common ones are customer-configured SSO and SCIM mappings (which are on the customer), and application-level logging you might need to enable. We flag these in the controls mapping so your auditors know owner responsibilities.
[06:43] Alex: Let's confirm next steps then.
[06:46] Maya: Action items: we'll send Trust Center access guide and link, Ethan will set up a demo for audit log export and KMS flow (EU), and you (Quantum Labs) will send a prioritized controls list or template so we can pre-map.
[06:57] Jordan: Sounds good. Can we do the demo next Wednesday?
[07:00] Ethan: I'm available next Wed 14:00 UTC; I'll follow up with calendar invite.
[07:05] Priya: One more question — is there any additional compliance evidence beyond SOC/ISO, like penetration test reports?
[07:10] Maya: We can provide a summary pen test report and remediation statements under NDA. We also publish a list of third-party attestations in the Trust Center.
[07:18] Alex: Great, thanks. We'll await the mapping sheet and demo invite.
[07:22] Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll email the artifacts and next steps.
[07:25] (call ends)
